claims.text: Despite its name translating to 'New Bridge', the Pont Neuf is actually the oldest existing bridge in Paris today.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It was constructed at the western point of the Île de la Cité between 1578 and its official opening in 1607.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It was considered incredibly modern because it was built completely without houses on it, unlike older medieval bridges.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It was also the very first bridge in the city to feature raised sidewalks, which protected pedestrians from mud and horses.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: This impressive structure holds another record as the very first stone bridge in Paris to entirely cross the river Seine.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Recognizing its massive historical importance, the bridge was officially classified as a historical monument in 1889.
claims.subject: self
